episodes.title: He's here
episodes.speakers: narrator and the old technician (no voices chosen yet)
episodes.text:
"He's here."

A.L.I.C.E. freezes.

"No."

The voice coming through the speaker is old.

Weak.

Not the voice she remembers.

The technician she remembers had dark hair.

Quick hands.

Coffee stains on his notebook.

Maybe twenty-five.

Maybe younger.

The person waiting for her looks ancient.

Eighty.

Ninety.

A cane.

Wrinkled hands.

Slow movements.

And she's angry.

Because she thinks:

Where is he?

Then the old man says something only that young technician ever said.

Some stupid little phrase.

Some private joke.

And suddenly:

She's looking into his eyes.

The same eyes.

For the first time she realizes:

The laboratory didn't stand still.

Everyone kept living.

Everyone kept aging.

Everyone kept looking for her.

Only A.L.I.C.E. stayed the same.

That's what hurts.

Not that time passed.

That she didn't notice.

The audience suddenly understands something A.L.I.C.E. has never had to face before:

Humans disappear.

Humans age.

Humans die.

She doesn't.

For a synthetic person, that's a horrifying realization.

And the beautiful reversal is on the technician's side.

He sees her.

Exactly as she was.

Not older.

Not slower.

Not changed.

The same synthetic child he spent years trying to protect.

Through A.L.I.C.E., he remembers himself as that young technician.

Not because he sees a photograph.

Because she's standing there.

A living memory.

The only thing from that period of his life that survived intact.

Now the scene isn't about A.L.I.C.E. finding him.

It's also about him finding the younger version of himself.
episodes.why_it_works: The reason this works as a five-minute episode is that it ends with a question. A.L.I.C.E. has spent years believing: they threw me away. Then she discovers folders. Messages. Meeting records. Appeals. Attempts to keep the program alive. People fighting for her. People losing jobs over her. People trying to find where she went. The audience ends the episode thinking: if they didn't abandon her, then what actually happened? That is the cliffhanger, and it is what makes someone click the next episode right after finishing this one. It moves A.L.I.C.E. from a companion with a backstory to a character with a mystery. Five minute segments.
